blocks.text: INN News - there's one important fact. Israel has never issued official documents, state speeches, or policies calling for the murder of all the Palestinian people. But no Israeli country rhetoric is driving Palestinian ethnic annihilation.

Instead, rhetoric hatred towards Israel and the Jews is very real. It's global, massive and religious. Hamas is an example. The Hamas Charter 1988 quote: "The End of Days will not come until the Muslims fight against the Jews and kill them..." That's not just politics. It's a sacred narrative.
Mahmoud al- Zahar, one of the founding of Hamas, has declared: "Kill him, for you cannot change the words of God. It's on television. It's undeniable.

This rhetoric doesn't stop in Palestine. It spreads to Europe, to America, to Asia. On the streets of London and New York, screaming from the river to the sea, Palestine will be free Echoing. It's clear: there is no Israel. There's no compromise room.

This is the difference. Israel talks about destroying Hamas, killing Palestine, not killing Palestine, and that violent rhetoric is meant for terror organizations, not ethnic. Hamas and his supporters speak of Jews as a nation and religion. The target is not a policy, but an existence.

The consequences of hatred rhetoric are great. For Jews, it ignites old trauma: the Holocaust, pogrom, banishment. For Israel, he closed the door of compromise. How do you negotiate with a public party to deny you your life rights?

This rhetoric is also a danger to the world. He triggered an attack on a Jewish community outside of Israel. Sinagoga burned. Jews were attacked on the street. In Western colleges, Jewish students are terrorized. Local conflict turned global hatred.
On the political side, hate rhetoric strengthens hard groups on both sides. Hamas is getting radical. Israel is getting suspicious. Modern voices are sinking. Peace is getting away.
From the legal side, an ethnic killing invitation can be read as a speech to genocide. But global politics keeps many parties silent. As a result, hatred is left normal.
From the perspective of strategy, this rhetoric only harms Palestinian struggle. The world sees, then asks: Is this about freedom or about Israel's removal? The sympathies were split.

Therefore, we must be clear. Israel can be severely criticized. But the claim that Israel called for the Palestinian massacre was incorrect. It's true: rhetoric hatred against Israel is real, vast and religious. This fact must be acknowledged if we want peace.

Peace is not born of lies. He was born of courage facing the truth. And the truth is clear: hate rhetoric is on the side that refuses Israel to live. If the world wants a way out, stop the legitimacy of hatred. Start with the words.
